title: Help
projectsDesc: Connect GitHub/GitLab repositories and set up AI to automatically handle tasks.
projectsStep1: Tap the + button at the top of the screen. (If no projects exist, there's also an 'Add Project' button on the empty screen.)
projectsStep2: If OAuth is set up, select a repo from the list. Otherwise, enter the repository URL and access token manually.
projectsStep3: Click 'Test Connection' to verify the repository is accessible.
projectsStep4: In label settings, click 'Create labels in Git' to create IVE workflow labels (IVE, IVE-S, IVE-D, etc.) in your repo. Defaults work fine.
projectsStep5: After saving, create at least one agent in the Agents tab — then any task you submit is auto-processed. (Agents live in your personal pool; no per-project assignment needed.)
projectsStep6: The project card shows stats: Waiting, Working, Verifying, Done, and Merge. Tap each number to open a detail panel.
projectsStep7: Use the ⏸ button to pause/resume the scanner, 🚀 to scan immediately, and + to add a task right from the card.
projectsTip: Tap the card to go to project settings. You can change scan interval, labels, and more.
agentsDesc: Manage both AI agents (auto-coding) and verifiers (human review) in one place.
agentsStep1: This tab shows two types: AI agents (auto-process tasks) and verifiers (humans who review AI results).
agentsStep2: Use the filter tabs (All / Agents / Verifiers) to view a specific type. The number next to Verifiers shows pending reviews.
agentsStep3: Tap + at the top to add an AI agent. Choose a CLI tool (Claude Code, OpenCode) and give it a name.
agentsStep4: Set the max turns — the number of AI conversation rounds the agent can use per task.
agentsStep5: Tap an agent card to expand details. Check Running/Done/Failed stats. Each agent automatically processes tasks you submit.
agentsStep6: Use 'Interview' to chat with the agent, or the stethoscope (🩺) to check CLI status.
agentsStep7: Verifiers are Git members assigned a review role in your projects — they appear automatically.
agentsTip: If agent status shows 'Offline', check CLI paths in Admin > Settings. Verifiers get a notification badge when reviews pile up.
issuesDesc: Register tasks and monitor AI processing in real-time.
issuesStep1: Select a project from the dropdown at the top of the screen.
issuesStep2: Tap the + button at the top to create one directly — first line becomes the title, rest is the body. Or add the target label (default: IVE) to a Git task for auto-detection.
issuesStep3: Agent assignment: 'Auto' picks from your agent pool via round-robin, or you can pick a specific one from your pool.
issuesStep4: Click a task to view execution logs, MRs/PRs, and comments in real-time.
issuesStep5: Use 'Bulk Edit' mode to select multiple tasks and change their status at once.
issuesTip: Task flow: Waiting → Dev → Verify Wait → Verifying → Done. Each stage is tracked automatically via Git labels.
reportsDesc: View processing stats, costs, and agent performance by period at a glance.
reportsStep1: Select Weekly/Monthly/Yearly at the top and use arrows (← →) to navigate periods.
reportsStep2: Check the briefing for totals, success rates, and costs. The flow chart shows inflow → waiting → throughput.
reportsStep3: Scroll down for agent workload, cost breakdown, task lifecycle, and per-project metrics.
reportsTip: Set up automatic report emails in Admin > Mail — configure schedule, time, and recipients.
adminDesc: Manage user permissions, CLI paths, mail, OAuth, and other system settings.
adminStep1: Users: Set per-user max agents, allowed CLI tools, and admin privileges.
adminStep2: Settings: Enter CLI executable paths (Claude Code, OpenCode). Agents use these paths to run AI tools.
adminStep3: Mail: Enter SMTP server info to enable automatic report delivery and notifications. Use the 'Test' button to verify.
adminStep4: OAuth: Register GitHub/GitLab OAuth apps so users can import all repositories in one click.
adminTip: Agents won't work if CLI paths are wrong. Always verify after configuration.
